press.framing.other: The paper reports that the public holds the other side responsible for beginning the war.
press.framing.own: The paper reports that the public holds its own side responsible for beginning the war.

reason.act-while-away: an act taken while Congress was away
reason.agency:nation-neutrality: the nation's own proclamation of neutrality
reason.charleston-command-succession: The local Confederate command passes to Colonel R. H. Anderson.
reason.fired-on-first: the public believes the other side fired first
reason.fugitives-held: border Unionists resent the holding of fugitives
reason.fugitives-returned: the Radicals and the abolitionists condemn returning people to slavery
reason.legislature-declines-secession: the legislature declares it has no power to secede
reason.military-authority-confirmed: The state forces are under Confederate military authority.
reason.military-convention-confirmed: The Virginia military convention places its military force at Confederate disposal.
reason.process-enforced: the army resents the court's process enforced against its officers
reason.ratification: Congress asked to ratify the acts taken while it was away
reason.recognition-letter: The War Department has addressed the government at Wheeling through its Governor.
reason.reorganisation-ordinance: The Wheeling convention has reorganised the government of Virginia.
reason.state-command-succession: State command passed to its recorded successor.
reason.state-forces-called-out: State volunteer forces recorded in service.
reason.state-forces-command: State command recorded in the military correspondence.
reason.state-forces-return: A later return supplies the contingent’s quantity.
reason.state-forces-tendered: State forces listed in the governor’s tender.
reason.state-forces-transferred: State forces transferred by the state’s own act.
reason.texas_original_deployment_ended: The original contingent?s deployment in Texas has ended under the existing departure agreement.
reason.writ-suspended: the writ of habeas corpus suspended on the military line
situation.arkansas_forces_transferred.te: Arkansas’s military board transfers the consenting state troops under the articles of 15 July: seven infantry regiments, one cavalry regiment, a cavalry battalion and five artillery companies. The articles retain the state’s clothing obligation for the men’s existing enlistments. The First in these State articles is Cleburne’s regiment.
situation.arkansas_secedes.text: The Arkansas convention has voted to secede, joining the slaveholding states already out of the Union.
situation.arkansas_secedes.title: Arkansas
situation.baltimore_route_closed.text: The railroad bridges north of Baltimore have been burned and the telegraph cut. No troops can reach Washington through the city.
situation.baltimore_route_closed.title: The route through Baltimore closed
situation.bates_fugitive_law_opinion.tex: Asked by a marshal in Kansas whether to serve in executing the fugitive slave law, Attorney General Bates answers: “It is the President's constitutional duty to 'take care that the laws be faithfully executed.' That means all the laws.”
situation.bates_fugitive_law_opinion.tit: The Attorney General on the fugitive slave law
situation.black_volunteer_offers.text: Black men in the North offer their service. In Washington, Jacob Dodson writes to the Secretary of War that he knows of “some 300 reliable colored free citizens of this city who desire to enter the service for the defense of the city”. On 29 April the Secretary of War replies: “this Department has no intention at present to call into the service of the Government any colored soldiers.”
situation.black_volunteer_offers.title: Black Northerners offer to serve
situation.blockade_or_closure.inaction: No blockade: the seceded states' trade by sea runs on.
situation.blockade_or_closure.option.und: Blockade in fact, without a proclamation
situation.blockade_or_closure.text: With the war begun, the cabinet divides on how to stop the seceded states' trade by sea.
situation.blockade_or_closure.title: A blockade or closed ports
situation.call_for_troops.inaction: No federal call: each governor acts on his own.
situation.call_for_troops.option.larger_: Call the militia, and three-year volunteers as well beyond the militia law, and answer to Congress later
situation.call_for_troops.option.militia: Call 75,000 militia for three months under the 1795 law, and summon Congress for 4 July
situation.call_for_troops.text: Fort Sumter has been fired on, and Congress is not sitting. The militia law of 1795 lets the president call out the militia of the states for three months.
situation.call_for_troops.title: The call for troops
situation.camp_jackson_deaths.text: Lyon's troops surrounded the state militia's camp outside St. Louis and marched its men under guard to the arsenal as prisoners. A crowd gathered along the way, and the troops fired. General Frost's protest says the fire killed some of his disarmed men and “several innocent lookers-on—men, women, and children”. Riots followed the next day.
situation.camp_jackson_deaths.title: The dead at Camp Jackson
situation.charleston_anderson_command.te: Colonel R. H. Anderson succeeds Beauregard in command of the Confederate forces at Charleston Harbor and its vicinity. The State volunteers remain under Governor Pickens.
situation.cherokee_neutrality.text: Principal Chief John Ross has proclaimed the Cherokee Nation's neutrality.
situation.cherokee_neutrality.title: The Cherokee Nation
situation.chickasaw_treaty.text: The government of the Chickasaw Nation has made a treaty with the Confederacy, together with the Choctaw Nation.
situation.chickasaw_treaty.title: The Chickasaw Nation
situation.choctaw_treaty.text: The government of the Choctaw Nation has made a treaty with the Confederacy, together with the Chickasaw Nation.
situation.choctaw_treaty.title: The Choctaw Nation
situation.confederate_capital_moved.text: President Davis arrived at Richmond on 29 May. Dispatches for the Confederate president now go there.
situation.confederate_commissioners.inac: No answer: they keep working through the Secretary of State's circle.
situation.confederate_commissioners.opti: File a refusal, hold back its delivery, and keep an unofficial channel through Justice Campbell
situation.confederate_commissioners.text: Commissioners from the seceded states are in Washington, seeking to be received. They are working through former senators and the Secretary of State.
situation.confederate_opening.option.red: Order General Beauregard to demand the fort's evacuation and, if it is refused, to reduce it
situation.confederate_opening.text: Fort Sumter is still held by a Federal garrison. The Secretary of War asks for orders to General Beauregard at Charleston.
situation.confederate_opening.title: Fort Sumter
situation.confederate_protection_act.tex: The Confederate Congress has passed “An act for the protection of certain Indian tribes”, and sent a commissioner to make treaties.
situation.confederate_protection_act.tit: An act of the Confederate Congress
situation.fort_monroe_arrivals.inaction: No instruction: each commander decides, and some go on returning people to slavery.
situation.fort_monroe_arrivals.option.ap: Do not give them up: employ them and keep account, their final status reserved
situation.fort_monroe_arrivals.option.re: Return them to slavery under the 1850 law
situation.fort_monroe_arrivals.text: The commander at Fort Monroe writes that more people have escaped to the fort from the Confederate works, and asks what to do with them and their families. The enslaver's claim, through Major Cary, is under the fugitive slave law of 1850.
situation.fort_monroe_arrivals.title: The people at Fort Monroe
situation.fort_monroe_escape.text: On the night of 23 May, Frank Baker, Shepard Mallory and James Townsend crossed Hampton Roads from the Sewell's Point works to Fort Monroe. Major John B. Cary, for their enslaver, has demanded them back under the fugitive slave law of 1850; General Butler has refused.
situation.fort_monroe_escape.title: Three men reach Fort Monroe
situation.fort_monroe_escape_asked.text: On the night of 23 May, Frank Baker, Shepard Mallory and James Townsend crossed Hampton Roads from the Sewell's Point works to Fort Monroe. Major John B. Cary, for their enslaver, has demanded them back under the fugitive slave law of 1850; the commander at Fort Monroe has asked for instructions.
situation.fort_monroe_escape_asked.title: Three men reach Fort Monroe
situation.gosport_yard.inaction: The commandant decides for himself what to do with the yard.
situation.gosport_yard.option.remove: Move the ships and guns out
situation.gosport_yard.text: Virginia's convention has voted to secede, and the navy yard at Gosport, by Norfolk, lies inside the state with its ships, guns and dry dock. Commodore McCauley commands it, and the state's militia are gathering.
situation.gosport_yard.title: The Norfolk navy yard
situation.habeas_on_the_line.inaction: The writ runs on the line, and the army's prisoners go before the courts.
situation.habeas_on_the_line.option.susp: Authorise the general-in-chief to suspend the writ of habeas corpus on the military line, where resistance makes it necessary
situation.habeas_on_the_line.text: Troops for Washington must cross Maryland, where the railroad bridges were burned and Baltimore is hostile. Anyone the army arrests along the line can be freed by the courts on a writ of habeas corpus.
situation.habeas_on_the_line.title: The writ on the military line
situation.harpers_ferry_assignment_notic: The War Department assigns Johnston to the troops near Harpers Ferry and directs him to arrange reinforcements through Lynchburg. This is an assignment, not a report of his arrival.
situation.houston_confederate_obligation: Writing for Governor Houston, Secretary of State E. W. Cave tells the Confederate War Department that the Governor does not recognise obligations to the Confederate government or the Convention’s authority.
situation.indian_territory_posts_given_u: The Army has withdrawn from its posts in the Indian Territory: Fort Washita, Fort Arbuckle and Fort Cobb.
The posts in the Indian Territory
situation.kentucky_neutrality.inaction: Kentucky stays closed to both sides until one of them moves.
situation.kentucky_neutrality.option.arm: Send arms quietly to Kentucky's Unionists
situation.kentucky_neutrality.text: Kentucky's House has resolved that the state take no part in the war except as mediator, and its governor forbids any movement on Kentucky soil. Kentucky Unionists ask for arms; the governors of Ohio and Illinois urge that the United States occupy Louisville, Covington and Columbus; General Scott answers that "thrusting protection upon their people is likely to do far more harm than good".
situation.kentucky_neutrality.title: Kentucky's neutrality
situation.kentucky_neutrality_proclaimed: Kentucky's governor has proclaimed the state neutral, closed to the troops of either side.
situation.lamon_promise.option.assure_no: Answer that the government will not try to supply Fort Sumter without giving the governor notice
situation.lamon_promise.text: Governor Pickens telegraphs that Colonel Lamon, the president's friend, told Charleston that Major Anderson's command would soon be withdrawn, and asks whether Lamon spoke for the government.
situation.lamon_promise.title: Colonel Lamon's word in Charleston
situation.manassas_advance_received.text: The Manassas command reports an enemy advance. Johnston can be directed to its assistance if practicable.
Beauregard’s report to the President requests reinforcements for his command at Camp Pickens. He describes unfinished defenses, poor equipment and a shortage of transport.
situation.maryland_legislature.text: Meeting at Frederick, the Maryland legislature has declared that it has no power to take the state out of the Union.
situation.maryland_legislature.title: The Maryland legislature
situation.mcclellan_proclamation.text: Crossing the Ohio, General McClellan issued his own proclamation to the people of western Virginia. It promised that his troops would not interfere with slavery, and that they would “with an iron hand, crush any attempt at insurrection on their part”: a rising by the enslaved.
situation.mcclellan_proclamation.title: McClellan's proclamation
situation.mcdowell_advance.inaction: No date is set, and the regiments' terms run out.
situation.mcdowell_advance.option.advanc: Advance now, before the terms run out
situation.mcdowell_advance.option.drill_: Wait and train the regiments first
situation.mcdowell_advance.text: The three-month regiments' terms run out in July. General McDowell's plan for an advance against the Confederate force at Manassas is before the president and the cabinet. McDowell asks for time to train his regiments; others press for a move before the terms expire.
situation.mcdowell_advance.title: An advance before the three-month men go home
situation.merryman_answer.inaction: The writ goes unanswered, and the suspension stands.
situation.merryman_answer.option.comply: Have the prisoner produced, and let the court's process be enforced on the line
situation.merryman_answer.text: The Chief Justice has sent the president a copy of his opinion in Merryman's case. "It will then remain for that high officer, in fulfilment of his constitutional obligation to 'take care that the laws be faithfully executed,' to determine what measures he will take to cause the civil process of the United States to be respected and enforced."
situation.merryman_answer.title: The Chief Justice's opinion
situation.merryman_writ.text: In Baltimore the Chief Justice has issued a writ of habeas corpus for John Merryman, arrested on 25 May and held by the army at Fort McHenry. The commander there, as the Chief Justice records it, "refuses to obey the writ of habeas corpus, upon the ground that he is duly authorized by the president to suspend it."
situation.merryman_writ.title: A writ for John Merryman
situation.minnesota_first_remuster.text: The First Minnesota has re-enlisted for three years, with service credited from its original muster.
situation.minnesota_first_remuster.title: The First Minnesota re-enlists
situation.missouri_arsenal.option.back_h: Back the department commander's course with the state
situation.missouri_arsenal.option.back_l: Back Lyon and enrol St. Louis's loyal volunteers
situation.missouri_arsenal.text: Missouri's governor has refused the call, and the state militia gathers near St. Louis. General Harney, commanding the department, seeks to keep the peace with the state; Captain Lyon and Representative Blair want to arm the city's loyal volunteers.
situation.missouri_arsenal.title: The St. Louis arsenal
situation.missouri_provisional_governmen: Missouri's convention has vacated the state's offices and installed a provisional government. The governor's government continues in the field.
situation.muscogee_treaty.text: The Creek Nation's commissioners have made a treaty with the Confederacy, signed by Principal Chief Motey Kinnaird and Icho Hacho, first chief of the Upper Creeks, among others. Opothleyahola is not among the signers.
situation.muscogee_treaty.title: The Creek Nation
situation.nelson_arrest_power.text: Judge Nelson of the Frederick County court telegraphs the commander at Relay House: “Send us five hundred men by first train, with power to arrest and disarm.”
situation.nelson_arrest_power.title: A Maryland judge asks for troops
situation.north_carolina_forces_transfer: North Carolina’s convention transfers its organized State troops by regiment under the ordinance of 27 June. Its provisions distinguish the war-term State troops from the four twelve-month volunteer regiments already in Confederate service and the additional 2,000 volunteers accepted.
situation.north_carolina_secedes.text: The North Carolina convention has voted to secede, joining the slaveholding states already out of the Union.
situation.north_carolina_secedes.title: North Carolina
situation.officer_resignation.text: The officer reports that he has resigned from United States service.
situation.officer_resignation.title: An officer resigns
situation.patterson_martial_law.text: From Philadelphia, General Patterson writes to the Adjutant-General: “it is expedient to declare or put the entire line, and ten, twenty, or thirty miles on each side, or the entire department under my command, under martial law; and if the General concurs, I ask his approval, or rather that he will give the order.”
situation.patterson_martial_law.title: General Patterson asks for martial law
situation.pickens_refusal_received.text: The Navy Department has received Adams’s letter declining to land Vogdes’s company under the Army order. Adams says that his Navy instructions still bind him to the truce.
situation.pickens_refusal_received.title: The Navy receives Adams’s refusal
situation.pickens_refused.option.courier: Send a Navy Department order to land the company, carried overland by special messenger
situation.pickens_refused.option.departm: Send a Navy Department order to land the company, by the usual ship
situation.pickens_refused.option.special: Sign a special expedition, drawn up outside the War and Navy Departments
situation.pickens_refused.text: Captain Adams has declined to land the company: he reads the order as breaking the January truce, and an Army order as no ground to set aside his Navy orders.
situation.pickens_refused.title: The Pickens order is not carried out
situation.pickens_reinforcement.inaction: The truce holds, and the fort is supplied by sea.
situation.pickens_reinforcement.option.l: Land Captain Vogdes's company from the ships
situation.pickens_reinforcement.text: Lieutenant Slemmer holds Fort Pickens under the January truce, with a company of troops waiting aboard Captain Adams's ships offshore.
situation.pickens_reinforcement.title: Fort Pickens
situation.pierpont_aid_requested.text: Pierpont has written to the President asking for military aid.
situation.pierpont_aid_requested.title: Pierpont asks for military aid
situation.pierpont_elected.text: The Wheeling convention has elected Francis H. Pierpont Governor of Virginia; he has taken the oath before the convention.
situation.pierpont_elected.title: Pierpont elected governor
situation.pratt_street_deaths.text: A crowd attacked the Sixth Massachusetts as it crossed Baltimore, and the soldiers fired. Four or five soldiers and nine to twelve civilians were killed; the accounts differ.
situation.pratt_street_deaths.title: The dead in Baltimore
situation.seward_memorandum.inaction: The paper is put away unanswered.
situation.seward_memorandum.option.answe: Answer that the policy is the president's to carry out
situation.seward_memorandum.text: The Secretary of State sends a paper: the administration has no policy at home or abroad, Sumter should be given up, and someone in the cabinet should direct policy.
situation.seward_memorandum.title: Some thoughts for the president's consideration
situation.special_session.inaction: Congress acts on its own; the spring's acts go unratified until it does.
situation.special_session.option.ask_war: Ask for 400,000 men and $400 million, and defend the spring's acts
situation.special_session.text: The House has met in special session. It will judge the acts of the spring, taken while Congress was away, and the president's message must say what the war needs.
situation.special_session.title: Congress meets
situation.sumter_evacuated.text: Major Anderson has surrendered Fort Sumter on the terms General Beauregard offered on 11 April: his command is allowed "the removal of yourself and command, together with company arms and property, and all private property, to any post in the United States which you may select", and may salute its flag.
situation.sumter_evacuated.title: Fort Sumter surrendered on terms
situation.sumter_fired_upon.text: The batteries at Charleston have opened fire on Fort Sumter.
situation.sumter_fired_upon.title: Fort Sumter fired on
situation.sumter_garrison.inaction: No decision: the garrison's provisions run down.
situation.sumter_garrison.option.give_up: Give up both forts, Sumter and Pickens
situation.sumter_garrison.option.provisi: Send provisions with warships, and give the governor of South Carolina notice
situation.sumter_garrison.text: Major Anderson's letters say his provisions will last only some weeks more, and that the fort cannot be relieved without a large force. The general-in-chief advises withdrawing the garrison.
situation.sumter_garrison.title: Fort Sumter's garrison
situation.tennessee_forces_receiving_pro: On 5 July Cooper directs Polk to arrange receiving with Harris and detail officers. Rolls are to be made and verified at the respective camps and stations before the designated officers receive them for future musters.
Confederate officers will verify Tennessee rolls
situation.tennessee_forces_return.text: Harris tenders twenty-two infantry regiments, two cavalry regiments and ten artillery companies on 2 July. He supplies unit counts and distinguishes stationary river batteries from field batteries still being prepared.
situation.tennessee_forces_return.title: Tennessee tenders its provisional army
situation.tennessee_forces_state_order.t: Harris later reported issuing this general order on 31 July, directing his officers to verify and deliver rolls when called upon and to hold their commands subject to Confederate orders. The original order and individual receipts remain unconfirmed; Benjamin later recognized 31 July for pay after muster.
Tennessee directs its officers to make their rolls available
situation.tennessee_forces_transferred.t: Tennessee’s General Assembly authorizes the governor on 29 June to place the state’s volunteer forces at the disposal of the Confederacy for muster into its service.
Tennessee authorizes a transfer of its volunteer forces
situation.tennessee_military_league.text: Tennessee’s military league of 7 May places its military forces and operations under the Confederate President’s direction, subject to ratification by both governments. The agreement supplies authority rather than a count of troops.
situation.tennessee_secedes.text: Tennessee's legislature has declared the state's independence, to be put to the voters on 8 June, joining the slaveholding states already out of the Union.
situation.tennessee_secedes.title: Tennessee
situation.texas_evacuation_terms.text: The February agreement yielded the posts in Texas while allowing the troops to retain their arms for the march to the coast. The department is arranging their departure.
situation.texas_evacuation_terms.title: Texas: the evacuation agreement
situation.texas_exit_1st_inf.text: The department?s original contingent is no longer available for field duty in Texas. The withdrawal begun under the February agreement has ended its original deployment.
situation.texas_exit_1st_inf.title: Texas: the original contingent leaves the theatre
situation.texas_exit_2nd_cav.text: The department?s original contingent is no longer available for field duty in Texas. The withdrawal begun under the February agreement has ended its original deployment.
situation.texas_exit_2nd_cav.title: Texas: the original contingent leaves the theatre
situation.texas_exit_2nd_cav_eg.text: The department?s original contingent is no longer available for field duty in Texas. The withdrawal begun under the February agreement has ended its original deployment.
situation.texas_exit_2nd_cav_eg.title: Texas: the original contingent leaves the theatre
situation.texas_exit_3rd_inf.text: The department?s original contingent is no longer available for field duty in Texas. The withdrawal begun under the February agreement has ended its original deployment.
situation.texas_exit_3rd_inf.title: Texas: the original contingent leaves the theatre
situation.texas_exit_8th_inf.text: The department?s original contingent is no longer available for field duty in Texas. The withdrawal begun under the February agreement has ended its original deployment.
situation.texas_exit_8th_inf.title: Texas: the original contingent leaves the theatre
situation.texas_governor_changed.text: The Convention has declared the Governor’s office vacant after Houston did not appear to take its oath. Its proceedings treat Lieutenant Governor Edward Clark as Governor that evening.
situation.texas_governor_changed.title: The Texas governorship
situation.thomson_martial_law.text: J. Edgar Thomson of the Pennsylvania Railroad writes to the Secretary of War: “As soon as the capital is safe from attack, it seems to me that the Government should at once turn on Baltimore and place it under martial law, and require that it should pay all damages”.
situation.thomson_martial_law.title: A railroad president on Baltimore
situation.townsend_fugitive_order.text: From the general-in-chief's headquarters, Assistant Adjutant-General Townsend writes to General Mansfield: “The general-in-chief directs that you take stringent measures to prevent any fugitive slaves from passing over the river particularly as servants with the regiments ordered over.”
situation.townsend_fugitive_order.title: The general-in-chief's order on fugitives
situation.virginia_forces_return.text: Virginia reports its aggregate organization. This paper does not give a separate return for each local contingent.
situation.virginia_forces_return.title: Virginia’s force return
situation.virginia_forces_transferred.te: Virginia has transferred its mustered volunteer forces to Confederate service. The existing contingents keep their identities and positions.
situation.virginia_harpers_jackson.text: Virginia has assigned Jackson to Harpers Ferry and relieved Harper and his militia. The volunteer companies now forming have no headcount in this order.
situation.virginia_harpers_jackson.title: Virginia state command changes
Harper reports about 2,400 men in all at Harpers Ferry. The militia share and original terms are not supplied.
situation.virginia_manassas_garland_retu: Cocke reports Garland's arriving force as 490 men. This dated return does not quantify Preston's battalion or establish a July strength.
situation.virginia_manassas_state_forces: Virginia reports a small force at Manassas. Garland's four-company battalion and Preston's seven-company battalion were ordered there on 10 May. Their headcounts and original terms are not supplied.
situation.virginia_military_convention.t: The War Department asks Virginia for the strength and rendezvous of its troops under the convention placing the state’s military force at the President’s disposal.
situation.virginia_norfolk_gwynn.text: The state command has a recorded successor. The change adds no troops and supplies no strength return.
situation.virginia_norfolk_gwynn.title: Virginia state command changes
situation.virginia_norfolk_huger.text: The state command has a recorded successor. The change adds no troops and supplies no strength return.
situation.virginia_norfolk_huger.title: Virginia state command changes
Virginia has placed the state troops assembled at Norfolk under Taliaferro. Their strength and original terms are not supplied.
situation.virginia_peninsula_state_force: The state command on the Peninsula has volunteer troops. Their headcount and original terms are not supplied.
situation.virginia_potomac_command.text: The state command on the Potomac is organizing its volunteer companies. No completed levy total is supplied.
situation.virginia_potomac_command.title: Virginia Potomac command
situation.virginia_richmond_magruder.tex: The state command has a recorded successor. The change adds no troops and supplies no strength return.
situation.virginia_richmond_state_forces: Virginia has assigned Johnston to its state forces in and about Richmond. Their strength and original terms are not supplied.
situation.virginia_secedes.text: The Virginia convention has passed an ordinance of secession, to be put to the voters on 23 May. It charges that federal power was “perverted” to the “oppression of the Southern slaveholding States”.
situation.virginia_secedes.title: Virginia
situation.virginia_state_calls.text: Virginia has authorized further volunteer companies at its rendezvous. An authorization is not a return of men already mustered.
situation.virginia_state_calls.title: Virginia calls more volunteers
situation.virginia_unionists.inaction: The president hears him and makes no offer.
situation.virginia_unionists.option.offe: Offer to give up Fort Sumter if the convention adjourns without seceding
situation.virginia_unionists.text: The Virginia convention, which voted 89 to 45 against a secession substitute on 4 April, is still sitting. At the Secretary of State's request, John B. Baldwin, a Unionist delegate, has come to Washington in place of George W. Summers.
situation.virginia_unionists.title: A Unionist from the Virginia convention
situation.washington_cut_off.inaction: The capital stays isolated until regiments find a route.
situation.washington_cut_off.option.arou: Bring troops around Baltimore by Annapolis
situation.washington_cut_off.option.meet: Meet the governor's request that no more troops cross Maryland
situation.washington_cut_off.text: With the route through Baltimore closed, the capital is isolated. Governor Hicks asks that no more troops cross Maryland.
situation.washington_cut_off.title: Washington cut off
situation.western_virginia.option.cross_: Order the Department of the Ohio across the river
situation.western_virginia.option.recogn: Recognise the Wheeling government as Virginia's
situation.western_virginia.text: Delegates from the western counties of Virginia have met at Wheeling against secession. General McClellan's Department of the Ohio lies across the river.
situation.western_virginia.title: Western Virginia
situation.wheeling_convention.text: Delegates from western Virginia have assembled in convention at Wheeling.
situation.wheeling_convention.title: The convention at Wheeling
situation.wheeling_legislature.text: The General Assembly of the government at Wheeling has met for its extra session.
situation.wheeling_legislature.title: The legislature at Wheeling
situation.wheeling_ordinance.text: The convention at Wheeling has passed an ordinance reorganising the government of Virginia. It provides for a governor and a legislature to assemble on 1 July.
situation.wheeling_ordinance.title: The Virginia government at Wheeling
situation.wheeling_recognition_letter.te: Cameron has addressed Pierpont as Governor of the Commonwealth of Virginia. Replying for the President to the application of 21 June, he promises additional troops and places federal recruiting agents under the Governor’s direction.
console.help.mandate: mandate paper-id           dispatch a declared assignment offered on this menu
console.error.mandate: Use mandate paper-id, naming a declared assignment offered on this menu.
